USMLE-style practice · Orthopedics

Crystals do not exclude infection

Choose the single best answer, then reveal the explanation.

A 70-year-old woman has fever and an acutely inflamed knee. Synovial analysis reveals urate crystals and many leukocytes. A trainee concludes that infection is excluded. Which response is most accurate while cultures are pending?

  1. Culture is unnecessary whenever crystals are present
  2. Only the serum urate level can diagnose joint infection
  3. Antibiotics are always forbidden in gout
  4. Crystal arthritis and septic arthritis can coexist
  5. Crystals sterilize synovial fluid
Reveal answer and explanation
Correct answer

Crystal arthritis and septic arthritis can coexist

Finding crystals does not rule out a concurrent joint infection.

Understanding the options

Crystal arthritis and septic arthritis can coexist
Finding crystals does not rule out a concurrent joint infection.
Crystals sterilize synovial fluid
Crystals do not eliminate microorganisms.
Culture is unnecessary whenever crystals are present
Microbiologic evaluation remains relevant.
Only the serum urate level can diagnose joint infection
Serum urate cannot establish or exclude septic arthritis.
Antibiotics are always forbidden in gout
Antibiotics are appropriate when a concurrent infection warrants them.
